ground_truth_question: What is the main purpose of BCG’s Global Data Classification Policy?
ground_truth_answer: The policy establishes a consistent, global framework for classifying BCG data so that appropriate protection and control levels are assigned to every data asset. It enables the firm to treat data as a strategic asset and to apply controls based on its business value, legal and regulatory obligations, and client commitments.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This Global Data Classification Policy (“policy”) establishes a framework for consistently classifying data globally and allows BCG to assign the appropriate level of protection and control to data or data assets (“data”).

ground_truth_question: Which security standard areas does this policy align to?
ground_truth_answer: The policy is aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, specifically to A.5.12 on classification of information and A.5.13 on labelling of information.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: ISO/IEC 27001:2022: A.5.12 Classification of information, A.5.13 Labelling of information

ground_truth_question: How does the risk statement describe why data classification is critical at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: The policy is presented as a critical component of BCG’s Global Information Security Program, ensuring protections and controls are applied based on the business value of data and that BCG meets organizational, client, legal, and regulatory obligations in the countries where it operates.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: The policy is a critical part of BCG’s Global Information Security Program treating data as strategic asset, applying protections and controls based on its business value and ensuring its compliance with organizational and client requirements, as well as fulfilling legal and/or regulatory requirements affecting the countries where BCG operates.

ground_truth_question: What does the Data Classification Framework help BCG do with its data?
ground_truth_answer: The framework organizes data into relevant categories so it can be used and protected more efficiently, and it makes data easier to locate and retrieve across the firm.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: The Data Classification Framework will allow BCG to organize data by relevant categories so that it will be used and protected more efficiently and makes data easier to locate and retrieve.

ground_truth_question: Who does this policy apply to across BCG?
ground_truth_answer: The policy applies worldwide to BCG employees, managing directors and partners, officers, suppliers, agents, external contractors, and any other person associated with BCG and its owned or controlled subsidiaries and affiliated entities, including Specialty Business Units.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: The policy applies worldwide, to all BCG employees, managing directors and partners, officers, suppliers, agents, external contractors, and other persons associated with Boston Consulting Group and its owned or controlled subsidiaries and affiliated entities (“BCG”), including Specialty Business Units (SBUs).

ground_truth_question: What is expected of BCG staff under this policy when handling data?
ground_truth_answer: All BCG staff must classify data using the policy’s defined data classification designations, ensuring consistent classification across the firm.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: BCG Staff will be required to classify all data at BCG using the Data Classification Designations set forth in this policy. This will ensure consistent classification across BCG.

ground_truth_question: How does the policy define data classification and on what factors are designations based?
ground_truth_answer: Data classification organizes data into designations for its efficient and effective use and to align with prescribed standards and controls. Designations are determined by the type of data, its characteristics, and its intended use.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Data Classification is the process of organizing data into designations for its most efficient and effective use and to ensure alignment with prescribed standards and controls. Designations are based on the type, characteristics and intended use of the Data.

ground_truth_question: What overall approach does BCG use to assign data classification designations?
ground_truth_answer: BCG applies a hybrid approach that combines content-based, context-based, and user-based methods to classify data.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: BCG will use a hybrid of the 3 methods to apply Data Classification Designations:

ground_truth_question: What is content‑based classification and how might it be applied?
ground_truth_answer: Content‑based classification assesses the subject matter of the data and applies a designation based on what the data contains. It can be applied manually by a data owner or automatically using algorithms, keywords, or phrases.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Content-based classification involves assessing the subject matter of the data being classified and applies classification based on this. This can be manual and applied by the data owner or automated based on algorithms, keywords, or phrases.

ground_truth_question: What is context‑based classification and what questions does it answer?
ground_truth_answer: Context‑based classification looks at the data asset, its location, and its creator as indirect indicators of sensitivity, without requiring user interaction. It addresses how the data will be used and who will access it and sets the classification accordingly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Context-based classification looks at data assets, location, and creator as indirect indicators of sensitive information, without user interaction. It answers the question of what the data will be used for, who will access it and then applies classification based on this,

ground_truth_question: When is user‑based classification required, and who is accountable for it?
ground_truth_answer: User‑based classification is used when automatic classification is not feasible. In these cases, end users must classify the data as they create and maintain it, and the data owner and their delegates are ultimately responsible for applying and validating the classification.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: User-based classification is required when automatic classification is not feasible and depends on manual Data Classification Designation by end-users while creating and maintaining Data. The data owner and their delegates are ultimately responsible for applying and validating a user-based classification.

ground_truth_question: Who determines the business value of data at BCG and what factors are considered?
ground_truth_answer: Each data owner or their delegates determine the business value of the data by assessing BCG’s and client requirements, legal and regulatory obligations, criticality, and sensitivity, including the business impact if the data is disclosed, altered, or destroyed.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Each BCG Data Owner or their delegates who generate or handle Data will determine the business value of the Data by assessing BCG’s and our client’s requirements, legal and regulatory requirements, criticality, sensitivity, including the business impact if the data is disclosed, altered, or destroyed

ground_truth_question: What are the four general data classification designations used at BCG (outside PRC‑specific rules)?
ground_truth_answer: Employees classify data as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted, using these designations to match protections to risk.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees will classify data into one of four possible classification designations: Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted

ground_truth_question: How is ‘Public’ information defined in BCG’s general classification scheme?
ground_truth_answer: Public information can be released to the public without confidentiality or privilege concerns and its unauthorized disclosure has no impact on BCG or its clients.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Public: Data which may be released to the public without any concern for confidentiality or privilege and with no impact to BCG. Unauthorized disclosure leads to: No impact on BCG Group and its clients.

ground_truth_question: What does the ‘Internal’ designation mean and what level of impact is associated with disclosure?
ground_truth_answer: Internal data should not be disclosed outside BCG and its unauthorized disclosure would result in minor or moderate impact to the firm, such as localized media attention or non‑public regulatory criticism.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Internal: Data whose unauthorized disclosure outside BCG would be inappropriate and would result in a minor or moderate impact to BCG. Unauthorized disclosure leads to: Minor/Moderate impact on BCG Group and its clients...

ground_truth_question: What does the ‘Confidential’ designation mean and what impact level is associated with it?
ground_truth_answer: Confidential data must be protected from unauthorized access or disclosure, whether internal or public. Its disclosure can have a major or extreme impact, including significant media attention and potential regulatory issues.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Confidential: Data which must be protected from unauthorized access or disclosure (both public and/or internal) ... whose disclosure has major or extreme impact to BCG.

ground_truth_question: What does the ‘Restricted’ designation require and what risk level does it reflect?
ground_truth_answer: Restricted data requires elevated or prescribed protections beyond those for Confidential data due to the very extreme impact that unauthorized disclosure could cause to BCG and its clients.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Restricted: Data which BCG must apply elevated or prescribed protections ... whose disclosure has a very extreme impact on BCG. These protections are applied in addition to those required for confidential data.

ground_truth_question: Which laws drive the PRC‑specific data classification scheme at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: BCG’s PRC scheme is adapted to the PRC Cybersecurity Law, the PRC Data Security Law, the PRC Personal Information Protection Law, and other applicable PRC regulations.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: PRC Cybersecurity and Data Protection Laws refer to the PRC Cybersecurity Law, the PRC Data Security Law, PRC Personal Information Protection Law and other applicable laws and regulations of the PRC.

ground_truth_question: What PRC‑specific classification designations does BCG use?
ground_truth_answer: For data subject to PRC laws, BCG uses Public, Non‑Sensitive, Standard, and Sensitive designations, adapting descriptions to PRC regulatory requirements.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees will classify data into one of four possible classification designations: Public, Non-Sensitive, Standard or Sensitive

ground_truth_question: What is the default classification for documents and emails established in the China environment, and can it be lowered?
ground_truth_answer: By default, documents and emails created in the China environment are classified as Standard, and that level cannot be lowered if PRC regulated data is involved or if a client prohibits cross‑border transfer of the data in those documents.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: By default, all word/excel/power point documents and emails established in China environment receive a designation of “Standard” that is not allowed to be lowered if (i) PRC regulated data ... is involved; or (ii) client prohibits cross-border transfer of data involved in such documents.

ground_truth_question: What does the PRC ‘Non‑Sensitive’ designation allow?
ground_truth_answer: Non‑Sensitive data can be stored and processed outside Mainland China and is used for projects that do not involve PRC regulated data or client‑restricted cross‑border transfers.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Non‑Sensitive: Data can be transferred outside of Mainland China • Applicable to data of projects that do not deal with PRC regulated data or data that is subject to client restrictions on cross-border transfer • Data can be stored and processed outside of Mainland China

ground_truth_question: What constraints apply to the PRC ‘Standard’ designation?
ground_truth_answer: Standard‑designated data must be stored in Mainland China and cannot be accessed or shared outside Mainland China. It applies to projects that deal with PRC regulated data or where clients restrict cross‑border transfers.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Standard: Data must be stored in Mainland China • Applicable to data of projects that deals with PRC regulated data or data that is subject to client restrictions on cross-border transfer • No access or sharing outside of Mainland China

ground_truth_question: When is the PRC ‘Sensitive’ designation used and what risks does it reflect?
ground_truth_answer: Sensitive is used when projects handle a large amount of, or highly sensitive, PRC regulated data. The data must be stored in Mainland China with no access or sharing outside Mainland China. Unauthorized disclosure could have a very extreme impact, and for data identified as important or core data, impacts could even endanger national security or public interests.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Sensitive: Data must be stored in Mainland China • Applicable to data of projects that deals with a large amount and/or highly sensitive PRC regulated data • No access or sharing outside of Mainland China ... For any sensitive Data which is identified by the PRC Cybersecurity and Data Protection Laws as important data or core data (if any), the impact may even include endangering China’s national security and public interest.

ground_truth_question: How can classification be applied at the case level in the PRC context?
ground_truth_answer: Classification can be applied to an entire case; all data processed in a case marked Sensitive shares that same Sensitive designation. For Standard and Non‑Sensitive cases, the default classification for all data is Standard, although individual documents may be reclassified if that default does not reflect their nature. Public classification does not apply at the case level.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Classification may be applied to an entire case. All data processed in “sensitive” cases share the same classification designation “sensitive”. The default classification of all data in “standard” and “non-sensitive” cases is standard (individual documents may be re-classified... ). “Public” classification does not apply to a case.

ground_truth_question: What does BCG mean by “PRC regulated data”?
ground_truth_answer: PRC regulated data refers to data subject to cross‑border transfer restrictions under PRC Cybersecurity and Data Protection Laws.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: PRC regulated data (which refers to data subject to cross-border data transfer restrictions under PRC Cybersecurity and Data Protection Laws)

ground_truth_question: Who is responsible for labelling data and what is the global default classification when no specific label is applied?
ground_truth_answer: Data owners and their delegates, authors, or system managers must mark all data according to its designation. Unless a different label is applied or required by law, the default classification is Confidential globally (and Standard for data subject to PRC laws).
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Data Owners and delegates, authors or system managers are required to mark all data according to its applicable designation... All data will have a default classification of Confidential (“standard” for data subject to PRC Laws) unless a different label is applied by the data owner or is required by law.

ground_truth_question: Will BCG provide practical guidance to help with labelling?

exact_excerpt_from_policy: BCG will publish and implement a set of Standards, Controls and Procedures to assist data owners and delegates, authors, and system managers in the labelling of their data.

ground_truth_question: What is the Data Asset Inventory and who oversees it?
ground_truth_answer: Data owners and their delegates must use and maintain a Data Asset Inventory for all data containing critical data elements that are collected, processed, stored, or transmitted by or for BCG. The inventory is maintained under the supervision of the Data Management Office.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: BCG´s data owners and delegates will use and maintain a Data Asset Inventory, under the supervision of the Data Management Office (DMO) for all Data containing critical data elements collected, processed, stored, or transmitted by or on behalf of the organization.

ground_truth_question: What kinds of details must the Data Asset Inventory capture?
ground_truth_answer: The inventory captures key data fields such as source, type, location, owner, retention, handling, and classification for each key data element.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This Data Inventory will include data fields like the source, type, location, owner, retention, handling, classification, etc. for each key data element.

ground_truth_question: If I’m classifying a dataset that combines multiple elements, which classification should I use?
ground_truth_answer: When classifying a collection used for a common purpose, you must apply the most restrictive designation of any individual element in the collection.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: When classifying a collection of data elements used for a common purpose or function, the data owner will apply the most restrictive designation of any of the individual data elements must be used.

ground_truth_question: Who is accountable for re‑evaluating classifications as business value changes over time?
ground_truth_answer: The data owner and their delegate must re‑evaluate designations to ensure they remain suitable, and any reclassification must be validated by the data owner or their delegate. For client data, the client case officer acts as the data owner.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: The business value of data may change over time, and it is the responsibility of the organization´s data owner and delegate to re-evaluate Data Classification Designation... Any data reclassification will be validated by the data owner or their delegates. In the instance of client data, the client case officer is acting as a data owner.

ground_truth_question: When creating a new document from an existing classified one (for example using “Save As”), how should classification be handled?
ground_truth_answer: When a new document is created from an existing asset, the data owner must consider the classification of the source data and apply an appropriate classification to the new document.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Creating new documents: When creating a new document or data asset from an existing document or data asset which is already assigned a classification (e.g., when using “save as” functionality), data owners must consider the classification of this data when saving and classifying the new document and apply the new classification accordingly.

ground_truth_question: What should I do if I copy content from one classified document into another?
ground_truth_answer: When copying data from an already classified document into an existing document, the data owner must consider whether the classification of the copied data requires changing the classification of the existing document and then apply the new classification accordingly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Copying data into existing documents: When copying data from an existing document or data asset which is already assigned a classification into an existing document, data owners must consider whether the classification of the copied data will result in a change in the classification of the existing document and apply the new classification accordingly.

ground_truth_question: How do changes in content, scale, or processing methods affect classification?
ground_truth_answer: If the content, scale, application scenario, or processing methods change, the data owner must consider whether those changes require a different classification and apply that new classification accordingly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Changes of data processing: When the content, scale, application scenario and processing methods of processed data change, data owners must consider whether such changes will result in a change in the classification of the document and apply the new classification accordingly.

ground_truth_question: How do new or updated laws and regulations influence classification?
ground_truth_answer: When relevant laws and regulations are introduced, such as industry guidelines for identifying critical data, data owners must identify affected data and apply the new classification accordingly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Changes of laws and regulations: When relevant laws and regulations are promulgated, e.g., guidelines for identification of critical data in related industries, data owners must identify the affected data and apply the new classification accordingly.

ground_truth_question: Does this policy change how long BCG retains data?

exact_excerpt_from_policy: This policy has no impact on data retention requirements, which are governed by BCG’s Global Data Retention Policy... Accurate classification is critical to ensuring appropriate retention periods.

ground_truth_question: What happens to documents that have not been classified or tagged?
